title: Pegboard spool holder: the A1's active spool, on the board
subtitle: One arm straight out of the board, spool face parallel to the board · 2 shared hook pegs + 4 pins (tools/pegboard.py) · your Menards 3/16" board · X out from the board, Z up · mm

meshes.label: Spool holder (2 hooks side by side, 4 pins 2" and 3" below, arm, end lip)
Reference 1 kg spool: 200 OD × 68 wide, 53 bore
Your board: Menards 3/16" white (6.35 mm holes, 3.94 mm thick)

scale_note: Real size. Pegs are the shared 6.1 mm hooks + pins. The spool is a typical 1 kg spool (200 mm across, 68 mm wide, 53 mm bore); the arm and lip pass through bores down to 50 mm and hold spools up to 82 mm wide.
notes: v4: the arm's top is now rounded (16 mm radius) instead of a flat with two chamfered corners. The spool's hole (25+ mm radius) rests on one smooth line along the top, so nothing sharp rubs the hub and the spool turns more evenly. The arc blends into 45° chamfers down the sides, so the bed side still prints without support. Strength is unchanged. Same as v3 otherwise: 2 hooks side by side, 4 pins 2" and 3" below; prints on its side with tree supports under the second peg column. Still to check: (1) which holes behind the A1 (the spool stands 74 mm out from the board, so it must clear the bed's travel); (2) whether the filament reaches the A1's PTFE tube.
